newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cardif backs Bancaire buyout offer.
newsitem.headline: Cardif backs Bancaire buyout offer.

text.p: Insurer and financial services firm Cardif said on Friday its board had recommended acceptance of an offer by parent Cie Bancaire to buy out the shares it does not already own.

The board which met on Thursday agreed the 900 francs per share offer, representing a 26 percent premium over the share price average for the past three months, was an attractive opportunity for shareholders, Cardif said in a statement.

Specialist retail financial services firm Cie Bancaire, majority-owned by financial group Paribas, announced plans on Wednesday to buy out its two units, Cardif and UFB Locabail, for a maximum three billion francs.
A Cie Bancaire spokeswoman said the transactions were aimed at "accelarating the improvement in its profitability".
Cie Bancaire said it would offer 900 francs per share for the 39.4 percent of Cardif in public hands and 600 francs for the 27.5 percent of UFB Locabail in the market.
Cardif finances business equipment and offers insurance while UFB Locabail is involved in insurance and savings.
